_comment: The profile for blog posts. Shares the pipeline with news; everything
that differs is here.
Component and layout are provisional until the export and the live schema are seen.
label: blog post

_comment: Blog posts land in a `blogs` folder rather than `news`.
The tree already carries one at every level, so nothing new is created.
Change the patterns here if the hierarchy differs further.
CONFIRM: where this type lives on aku.edu -- the SOURCE, not the target.
These two are easy to conflate and are not the same thing. `hierarchy.leaf`
is where an item lands in Storyblok. This is where it came from: the path
SharePoint serves it under, the detail page its internal links point at, and
the shape of the id in those links (news_details.aspx?nid=NEWS-1234).
They coincide for news, which is exactly why the /news in build_link_map.py
went unnoticed. For blogs and events the values below are a GUESS -- check a
real internal link in the export before the first run, or every cross-link
will simply fail to resolve and be left pointing at aku.edu.
CONFIRM before the first upload: the component a blog post becomes may
not be news_article, and its body whitelist may differ. Reading the
live space is the only way to know -- see
pipeline/migrate/review/dump_sb_tree.py and fetch_storyblok_space.py.
storyblok._confirmed: blog_article exists in the space (id 205045811148991); read off the live schema, not guessed
_schema_note: blog_article gained four fields on 10 Aug: thumbnail, isGlobal, isFeatured
and category. That closes four of the six gaps this profile was written
isFeatured and category are CUSTOM plugin fields (featured-plugin,
category-plugin) and no story in the space has either filled, so the value
format they expect is not knowable from the data. Ask the dev before
writing to them -- a guess here is a guess repeated 83 times.

_comment: How source content maps onto components. Signed off against the
reference story; see docs/PROJECT.md section 5.
spacing is mandatory on every blok -- three values, by component. A blok
without one renders with no vertical rhythm at all.
The real column names of the AKU Blogs list, read off the export rather
than assumed. They share almost nothing with the News list: the body is
'Blog Detail', the title 'Blog Title', and there is no City column at all,
which is what news derived region from.
Verify after any re-export:  python pipeline/new_type.py blogs --check
fields.title: Blog Title
fields.author: AuthorName

_content_fields_comment: The blogs story payload. Deliberately NOT a copy of news's 44 keys: the
blogs list has 26 columns, two of them empty on all 83, and none of news's
alternate-language, approver or globally-active fields exist at all.
Declaring only what the export actually has means a null in a built payload
is a real absence rather than a column nobody mapped.
field:    a logical name from `fields`, resolved per content type
_skip_steps_comment: Steps blogs does not need. News had to read all 3,606 live pages to work
out which file was a story's banner, because the export renamed
everything. Blogs name the file directly in the Banner column and all 70
are already on disk, so these two have nothing to work out.
NOT skipped: the 37 inline body images are still SharePoint paths and do
need fetching, so the richtext-media steps stay.
_authors_note: Author biographies and photos are NOT in the delivered export. They live in
a SharePoint list called AuthorManagement, which AKU did not send alongside
categories.json and entities.json -- it was found by asking the site which
data/source/author_photos.json  author id -> photo file, 6 matched
Coverage across the 83 blogs: 76 have a bio, 6 have a photo. Two author ids
used by posts (4 and 5) are not in the list at all.

_comment: Signed off by the content owner on 2026-08-11. Each entry says what was
decided and why, so a later reader does not reopen a settled question.
Anything still 'pending' is waiting on the named party, not on us.

tags.note: 47 distinct values, no field on blog_article. Held until the dev confirms whether a field is coming. Data is kept in the payload either way, so nothing is lost by waiting.

post_year.note: NOT redundant with `date`, which was the reason to consider dropping it. 76 of 83 match the year of the publish date, but 7 do not: blogs 33, 34, 35, 46, 47, 66 and 67 are December posts filed under the FOLLOWING year. It is an editorial issue-year, not a calendar year, so deriving it from `date` would misfile those 7. No field exists yet; kept in the payload and in backup/raw.

shared_entities.note: Place in the regions/<region>/entities/<entity>/blogs structure and share to the rest through `entities`. The physical region is a judgement call — blogs have no City column and these five name an entity that exists in several regions. See shared_placement below.

thumbnail.note: Leave empty. No source exists in SharePoint and the signed-off reference story leaves it empty too.

is_active.note: 82 of 83 are True. Blog 37, '40 years of AKU', is False — it is the only post that is switched off in SharePoint. Kept so that a deliberately unpublished post is not silently published.

close_comments.note: 14 posts have comments closed. The dev has confirmed a suppression field is coming; until it lands comment_form cannot be hidden.

feature_sequence.note: 45 posts carry an order (33 are '1', 5 are '2', 4 are '3', 3 are '0'). No field, and featured-plugin's value format is still undemonstrated, so ordering cannot be expressed yet.

post_comments.note: 626 comments on the site, no field and no component. Not migrated. They remain in backup/raw/ if AKU ever asks for them.

embeds.note: Do not use a raw iframe. Blog 18 is the only post with either field: its Embed Video is a YouTube URL -> media_section with type=video; its Embed Code is a Facebook post -> social_embed with variant=facebook. social_embed also replaces the iframes news used for Twitter — variants are twitter, facebook, instagram.

_comment: Where the five multi-region blogs physically live. `entities` still lists
EVERY region's folder for that entity, so the post is reachable from all
of them; this only decides the one folder it is stored in.
Evidence is thin and is stated per post. Change a value here and rerun
